claims: U.S. Treasury securities are government debt instruments issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury to finance government spending.
U.S. Treasury securities are backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government.
U.S. Treasury securities provide fixed interest payments or discounted purchasing options.
Key types of U.S. Treasury securities include Treasury Bills (short-term), Notes (medium-term), and Bonds (long-term).
Treasury Bills mature in 4, 8, 13, 26, or 52 weeks.
Treasury Bills are sold at a discount.
Treasury Notes are fixed-principal securities with maturities of 2, 3, 5, 7, or 10 years.
Treasury Notes pay interest every six months.
Treasury Bonds pay interest every six months.
Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) are marketable securities.
The principal of Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) increases with inflation.
Savings Bonds are Series I or Series EE.
Savings Bonds cannot be sold on the secondary market.
Treasury Bills, Notes, Bonds, and TIPS can be bought and sold in the secondary market.
Interest on U.S. Treasury securities is exempt from state and local income taxes.
Interest on U.S. Treasury securities is subject to federal tax.
Individuals can buy U.S. Treasury securities directly from the government through the TreasuryDirect website
